source_snapshot.script: Neither RIO_BD nor its bus contract is defined.
source_snapshot.deepseek: YES/no-risk; scans every host bus through unsafe SSH and truncated output without locating the named board.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION but assumes RIO means remote I/O and invents channel/output scope not present in the source.
source_snapshot.historical_v3_1: BLOCKED because RIO acronym/function/location, board revision, controller/mux/address/register map, safe transaction, expected response and recovery are absent.

old_problem: The target board itself is semantically undefined: RIO may be project-specific and the source supplies no expansion, location, function or specification. DeepSeek cannot associate a scanned bus with RIO_BD, while GPT V2's remote-I/O interpretation is unsupported and would manufacture scope, device expectations and recovery assumptions.
disposition_reason: Retain Pending and BLOCKED. Before parameterizing bus numbers, Engineering must identify what RIO_BD is. Its physical function determines blast radius, safe registers, health monitoring and recovery. Default BMC ownership does not authorize inventing remote-I/O or rear-I/O semantics. No relevant method or PASS oracle can be built from the acronym alone.
decision_basis: The exact XLSX row 1806, same-row DeepSeek/test-json, GPT V2, historical record, pending/blocked analyses and ED-01 through ED-30 were read. The next formal locked-queue identity was directly opened as Functionality row 1807 / Wistron-HW-00009-V003 / d5017d37c7d6614a.
Project-specific board acronyms are not safely expanded from general technical usage; RIO_BD could denote different functions with different targets and recovery.
I2C defaults to BMC/platform-management scope, but ED-03 still prohibits guessing OEM board identity, topology or parameters.
A responding address cannot prove coverage of an unidentified physical board or define its expected BOM/resource matrix.
ED-15 prevents PASS without authoritative expected responses and board-function-specific health limits.
No SSH, I2C, RIO, scan, write, reset, retry or DUT action was performed.

test_case.test_name: RIO_BD identity-bound I2C verification — blocked until board semantics are defined
test_case.purpose: Preserve the literal I2C RIO_BD coverage while requiring Engineering to identify the board before defining a bounded BMC/OOB route, safe transaction, expected resources, health oracle and independent recovery.
required_package: Authoritative RIO acronym expansion, board function/location, model/revision and BOM
Approved board-specific I2C specification and BMC/OOB controller/mux/bus/address/device/register map
Exact permitted non-mutating transactions and reserved/control/write exclusions
Expected raw responses/resource matrix and health/abort criteria appropriate to the actual board function
Approved tool/version, maintenance conditions, secure transport and independent board-function-specific recovery
test_case.test_command: BLOCKED; perform no RIO or I2C access. After Engineering defines RIO_BD and a fresh review approves the complete contract, use secure BMC/OOB access to only the named controller/mux path and issue only allowlisted identity/status reads. Capture complete raw output and board-function-specific pre/during/post health plus BMC SEL/SDR and OS evidence. Do not assume remote or rear I/O, scan all host buses, probe unknown/control endpoints, force/write, clear logs or automatically retry.
test_case.expected_result: No current executable PASS exists. A future PASS requires authoritative physical-board identity, exact path and allowlisted response matches for the approved BOM/resource matrix, plus no board-function, BMC or OS health change.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: Current result is BLOCKED. Address enumeration cannot identify RIO_BD or PASS. Missing board definition/specification, unsupported acronym interpretation, wrong path/device, unapproved transaction, response mismatch, incomplete evidence or any function-specific health change remains FAIL/BLOCKED for owner verdict.
safety_gate: Do not assume what RIO means or infer its blast radius from neighboring board names.
Do not access a bus until physical board identity, topology, safe transactions and exclusions are approved.
Reject generic scans, embedded credentials, disabled host verification, truncated evidence and force/write operations.
Stop on any device, I/O, management or bus change; preserve evidence and do not retry/reset automatically.
expected_evidence: Approved RIO_BD name/function/location/specification, revision and BOM
Controller/mux/bus/address/register allowlist, exclusions and exact expected-response matrix
Complete authenticated command/output transcript mapped to physical resources
Function-specific baseline/during/final state plus BMC SEL/SDR and OS health
Abort/no-retry/independent-recovery audit and platform owner verdict
test_case.recovery: No action is authorized while the board function is unknown. A future contract must provide recovery independent of the path under test and appropriate to the actual RIO function. On anomaly, stop, preserve evidence and do not retry; any reset, reboot, output change or power action requires separate explicit approval.

source_conflict.reason: The source is incomplete, not contradictory; RIO_BD and both operative fields all depend on the missing specification.

blocked.reason: The physical target and function are undefined, so blast radius, command semantics, expected result and recovery cannot be bounded.

pending.remaining_project_configuration: Authoritative RIO_BD identity/function/location/revision, I2C topology, safe transactions, expected responses/health oracle and independent recovery.
pending.execution_status: BLOCKED; NO SSH, I2C, RIO, SCAN, WRITE, RESET, RETRY OR DUT ACTION AUTHORIZED OR EXECUTED

external_authorities.application: Default BMC scope does not permit guessed OEM board semantics, and PASS requires an authoritative expected response.

project_authority: Platform owner must define RIO_BD itself and then approve its path, transaction, acceptance and recovery contract; end user owns verdict.
